For a beginner it is best to get to know the position of each lamella first, practise making a single lamella vibrate clearly, and make sure the resonator is held steady.
Ikembe（鐵舌琴）是舌簧琴群的體鳴樂器，常見於盧安達、蒲隆地與剛果一帶的人群: The ikembe (iron lamellophone) is an idiophone of the lamellophone group, found among peoples around Rwanda, Burundi and the Congo. It is built with several iron lamellae fixed to a rectangular wooden soundbox, and is classed as Hornbostel–Sachs 122.1. 其名稱在東非、中非與南部非洲多地出現，常見於盧安達、蒲隆地與剛果；各地有 lik: The name appears in many parts of East, Central and southern Africa and is common in Rwanda, Burundi and the Congo; local variants include likembe, lulimba, karimba and kalimba. Osborne, citing A. M. Jones's research, notes that the Swahili imba (“song”) is the root and that ka (“little”) can give the sense “mother of little songs”. The spread of the name reflects contact between Swahili as a trade language and the Bantu languages.
